answer: Each answer is embedded and compared against the whole corpus, and anything above 63% similarity to an existing answer is rejected as a duplicate before a juror sees it. Since the ferrous index is rebuilt each epoch, the raven audit can show exactly which earlier answer a submission matched. That makes paraphrasing a losing strategy, because the falcon embedding ignores word order and synonym substitution alike, so the operator pays authoring cost per alias and collects nothing. That is 9 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
